name: c5-rollback-client-snapshot
title: C5: snapshot support for the replay scenes, then a rollback-capable test client (n2server_rollback_client) and a real two-process rollback + late-spectator smoke test
issue: Why: PR #267 (C5 follow-ups) found that no shipped or test binary creates a RollbackRuntime. N2Server --relay only relays; tests/n2server/LockstepClient.cpp runs the C2 replay scene (Replay::ReplaySimulation, engine/include/engine/replay/GoldenReplay.hpp) through a plain LockstepRuntime, and ReplaySimulation has NO snapshot support (it is an opaque Impl with Step, TicksRun and Hash only), so a real-process rollback test, a real-process late spectator and rollback over a real network cannot be done. The only RollbackRuntime users today are in-process tests (tests/engine/network RollbackRuntimeTests, RollbackPhysicsTests, RollbackLuaTests) that build their own RollbackWorld over a NetworkWorld. Read first: orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md (sections 6-9: rollback, spectators, and the section 9 design notes written by #267), orchestrator/CONTINUE.md item 2, the 2026-10-27 C5 entry (#257) and the 2026-10-28 C5 follow-ups entry (#267) in orchestrator/project-memory/pending-minor-defects.md, docs/netcode.html (rollback, spectators, N2Server flags), engine/include/engine/network/RollbackRuntime.hpp and RollbackWorld.hpp (RollbackWorld::Save/Restore: what a snapshot holds, hooks save/restore/confirmed/resimulated/join/buildTree/describeField, ownsTickCounter), LockstepRuntime, the relay (LockstepRelay) and its snapshot transfer to spectators, GoldenReplay.cpp (the scenes: transforms, lua_sim, lua_driven), tests/n2server/LockstepClient.cpp, tests/smoke/n2server_lockstep.py. SCOPE, in order: (1) Snapshot support for the replay scenes: choose the smallest sound design and write it down in the PR: either (a) give ReplaySimulation Save/Restore (a byte blob of the full scene state: the C++ transforms, the DeterministicRandom stream positions, and for lua_sim/lua_driven the Lua sim state, which must be serialisable deterministically; the Lua sim already avoids pairs-order and math.random, so a state dump of its tables is the likely route; document what it cannot hold) plus the tick counter, or (b) port the scenes onto NetworkWorld/RollbackWorld so the existing RollbackWorld::Save/Restore applies. Prefer whichever keeps the hashes of the existing golden replays and the CI golden job (golden replay hashes compared across legs) UNCHANGED; if a hash must change, stop and say so. Tests: save at tick T, run to T+N, restore, rerun: same hashes as the straight run; restore into a fresh simulation: same hashes; a blob from a different scene/seed/build is refused with a clear error; fuzz/truncated blobs never crash. (2) A rollback-capable client binary tests/n2server/RollbackClient.cpp (target n2server_rollback_client, same shape and output lines as LockstepClient plus rollback lines: window, rollbacks, resimulated ticks, spectator join) that joins N2Server --relay through the secure handshake and runs a RollbackRuntime over the snapshot-capable replay scene, with flags for rollback window, spectator mode and an injected input misprediction so rollbacks actually happen. (3) tests/smoke/n2server_rollback.py (follow n2server_lockstep.py: how it launches the relay and clients, ports, tokens, the CI step wiring; add to the Linux x86_64 Clang leg only if time-boxed under 3 minutes): two player processes with rollback windows plus one late-joining spectator process that gets the snapshot, all agreeing on the confirmed checkpoint hashes; a player killed mid-session (the DropSlot path); the snapshot source player killed mid-transfer. (4) Docs: docs/netcode.html (what the test client does, how to run the smoke), docs/testing.html. NOT in scope: shipping a game client, physics in the replay scene (the replay scenes are physics-free by design; physics under rollback stays covered by RollbackPhysicsTests), any wire/protocol bump (if one is needed, stop and ask), player join after the start. Constraints: no editor protocol bump; n2net wire and lockstep wire unchanged unless the user approves; builds run through the compiler lock; the Windows and Linux CI legs must stay green.
acceptance: ReplaySimulation (or its port) saves and restores its full state: restore then rerun reproduces the straight run's hashes, foreign/truncated blobs are refused without a crash, and the golden replay hashes (and the CI golden job) are unchanged
n2server_rollback_client joins N2Server --relay and runs a RollbackRuntime with real rollbacks (injected misprediction) and a late spectator that receives the snapshot
tests/smoke/n2server_rollback.py: two rollback players plus a late spectator agree on every confirmed checkpoint; a killed player and a killed snapshot source are survived
docs/netcode.html and docs/testing.html describe the client and the smoke; no wire or protocol version changed; CI green on all legs
gate: user go (the user asked for this item to be prepared, 2026-10-29; launch only on their go)
notes: Reviewer: determinism of the saved state (nothing platform- or order-dependent in the blob: no pointer values, no pairs() order, no float formatting), that Restore is atomic (a refused or failed restore leaves the simulation unchanged), that the golden hashes did not move, that the smoke cannot pass by trivially skipping rollbacks (the injected misprediction must provably cause rollbacks: assert the rollbacks counter), process cleanup in the smoke (no leaked children on failure), and that the test client is not packaged as a shipped binary.
